cards.label: ACT
cards.claim: Existing precision Casimir setups could search for axion-mediated spin-dependent forces by comparing reversed polarisations of a magnetically compensated source.
cards.people: Xiaolin Ma, Volodymyr Takhistov, Hideo Iizuka; report numbers KEK-QUP-2026-0020 and KEK-TH-2887 suggest a KEK affiliation, individual affiliations not in source
cards.stage_headline: Stage 1 of 5: an idea, not yet tested.
cards.stage_note: This is a proposal with sensitivity projections. No experimental partner or demonstration run yet.
cards.impact_heading: IF IT WORKS, HOW BIG A DEAL?
cards.impact_text: It would give existing Casimir hardware a new, cleanly falsifiable use. The projected reach on g_p^e g_s^N and g_p^e g_s^e at λ ~ 1–100 µm is described as orders of magnitude beyond existing lab searches.

details.heading: What the work shows
details.text: The spin force reverses sign under the polarisation flip while Casimir, gravitational and electrostatic backgrounds "broadly cancel". No shielding is needed, so large probes can work at micrometre gaps.

details.heading: Still unknown
details.text: How well the cancellation holds in practice, given patch potentials and imperfect magnetic compensation. No experimental group is attached yet.

details.heading: Would make it more convincing
details.text: A named Casimir group committing to a demonstration with a pre-specified systematics budget.

details.heading: Would prove it wrong
details.text: Systematics in a demonstration run that do not reverse with the polarisation flip and exceed the projected signal.

cards.todo: Email Takhistov and ask whether an existing Casimir group has signed on.
cards.rule_text: Scope seed funding only if a named experimental group commits to a demonstration with a pre-specified systematics budget.
cards.compare_text: Read alongside Quanta's Nov 25 piece on new ultralight dark-matter searches. This is journalism and a lead only, not a benchmark.

cards.label: WATCH
cards.claim: Polarisation angles of radio galaxies at z≈0.5 show a rotation that matches the CMB birefringence hint in sign and size.
cards.people: Marcus Brüggen, Jorinde Dreismann, Pranjal Trivedi, Shane P. O'Sullivan, Takuya Akahori, Fumihiro Naokawa, Cameron L. Van Eck, Marco Regis et al.; affiliations not in source
cards.stage_headline: Stage 3 of 5: tested against a control.
cards.stage_note: The fit tests rotation against zero using a population model, on radio data with systematics independent of the CMB. The radio result alone is only ~1.4σ, so this is not yet a replication.
cards.impact_heading: IF TRUE, HOW BIG A DEAL?
cards.impact_text: A rotation in the last ~5 Gyr would point to a late-evolving field such as axion-like dark energy. Axion-like dark matter acting before reionisation predicts β≈0 at these redshifts.

details.heading: What the work shows
details.text: The study uses 33,298 components of 16,649 POSSUM double radio sources, and a χ₀−ψ≈0° population that halves the variance. Radio only: β = 0.48° ± 0.35° (~1.4σ). Combined with ACT+Planck: 0.282° ± 0.056° (5.0σ). The title's "confirms" is too strong: the CMB alone gives 0.277° ± 0.057° (4.8σ), so the radio data are consistent with the CMB, not a confirmation.

details.heading: Still unknown
details.text: POSSUM's absolute polarisation-angle calibration, which the authors say is needed. Also unknown: whether residual Faraday rotation or source-morphology systematics could produce ~0.5°.

details.heading: Would make it more convincing
details.text: The full POSSUM survey with absolute angle calibration reaching ≥3σ from radio alone, plus a tomographic split by redshift.

details.heading: Would prove it wrong
details.text: A calibrated full-survey radio β consistent with 0 at ~0.1° precision. That would rule out late-time rotation, but not rotation before reionisation.

cards.todo: Read the paper now; no outreach yet.
cards.rule_text: Contact only if the POSSUM team publishes an absolute-angle calibration plan or a full-survey β with radio-only σ ≤ 0.15°.
cards.compare_text: Joint ACT+Planck β = 0.277° ± 0.057°. The combined 5.0σ result rests almost entirely on this CMB figure.

cards.label: WATCH
cards.claim: DESI's evolving dark energy can be reinterpreted as the effect of inhomogeneous geometry in ordinary general relativity, with no dark-energy fluid.
cards.people: Thomas Buchert; affiliation not in source
cards.stage_headline: Stage 2 of 5: uses data, but no comparison group.
cards.stage_note: The paper uses DESI data to fix the averaged budget. No head-to-head comparison with a dark-energy model was seen.
cards.impact_heading: IF TRUE, HOW BIG A DEAL?
cards.impact_text: It would remove the need for dark energy.

details.heading: What the work shows
details.text: The total geometric budget that replaces dark energy is "pinned five times better" than the split between backreaction and curvature. The author presents this as the backreaction counterpart of DESI's evolving-dark-energy evidence.

details.heading: Still unknown
details.text: Whether the required backreaction size is physically achievable; most N-body/GR studies find it small. The split with curvature is also poorly constrained.

details.heading: Would make it more convincing
details.text: A formal model comparison against dark-energy fits, and a reproduction of S₈ ≈ 0.77 as well as the distances.

details.heading: Would prove it wrong
details.text: Relativistic simulations or a curvature measurement showing backreaction far below the needed size.

cards.rule_text: Revisit when a model-comparison paper or a relativistic-simulation test appears.
cards.compare_text: HSC-Y3 shear finds S₈ ≈ 0.77 and says the dynamical-dark-energy signal is driven mainly by distances. Any dark-energy-free explanation must match both.

cards.label: CONTEXT
cards.claim: A civil air-surveillance radar recorded 8 unresolved detections over 84 s at an estimated 55,000–70,000 ft over North America in 2023.
cards.people: DoD PURSUE release 8, file DOW-UAP-D165; covered by EarthSky on Nov 22
cards.stage_headline: Stage 2 of 5: uses data, but no comparison group.
cards.stage_note: This is sensor data with official analysis, but there is no comparison case. Released one day before the window.
cards.impact_text: It is one of the few release items with sensor data and official analysis. However, the analysis itself cannot show that the detections are a single object.

details.heading: What the release shows
details.text: If one object made all 8 detections, it moved at about 1,650 mph (~Mach 2.5) and changed bearing by ~39°. The analysis says the 12-second sweep interval cannot establish one object or a continuous track.

details.heading: Would make it more convincing
details.text: Raw radar returns, data from other sensors at the same time, and a check of false-track rates for that radar.

details.heading: Keep in mind
details.text: Release 8 has 43 files (40 documents, 3 videos), mostly a mix of old and new material.

cards.rule_text: Revisit only if a release includes multi-sensor raw data.

cards.label: CONTEXT
cards.claim: Huw Price argues that recent work shows many 1989 critics of cold fusion were wrong, in a reply to George Musser's Quanta coverage.
cards.people: Huw Price, 3 Quarks Daily; affiliation not in source
cards.stage_note: This is an essay replying to journalism. It makes no new experimental claim.
cards.impact_text: It frames the current LENR debate. The gap between enhanced cross-sections and measurable excess heat is the key benchmark for any LENR proposal.

details.heading: What he says
details.text: Many 1989 critics were wrong. He also cites Metzler et al., who note that far more than a 10¹⁸ enhancement would be needed for measurable excess heat.

details.heading: Keep in mind
details.text: This is pushback on journalism, not on a scientific claim. No LENR primary research appeared this week.

cards.compare_text: Nature Communications (2026) reports materials-dependent enhancement of low-energy fusion in solids. It says such fusion rates are not presently relevant for energy production.

compare_link.label: Enhanced nuclear fusion in the sub-keV energy regime ↗

cards.label: BENCHMARK
cards.claim: There is no convincing broadband 2–4 GHz technosignature from 210,191 Gaia DR3 main-sequence stars within 100 pc across all VLASS epochs (2017–2026).
cards.people: Steve Croft (Oxford University / UC Berkeley / SETI Institute)
cards.stage_headline: Stage 3 of 5: tested against a control.
cards.stage_note: Detections are compared against the expected rate of chance coincidences.
cards.impact_text: It sets a new population-wide limit on wideband transmitters. The median per-star limit on steady emission is L_ν < 4.0×10⁸ W Hz⁻¹.

details.heading: What the work shows
details.text: In the Epoch-1 catalogue there were 51 high-reliability positional matches against 1.5 expected by chance. Each is judged plausibly noise, a background source or stellar emission, and none warrants priority follow-up.

details.heading: Check when reading
details.text: How "51 vs 1.5" fits with the statement that counted detections are "no more numerous than chance". Presumably most matches are ordinary stellar radio emission, but this is unconfirmed. The faintest late-M and substellar objects are excluded.

details.heading: Keep in mind
details.text: This is a limit, not a claim. Any future wideband candidate must exceed it.

cards.todo: Store as a benchmark limit for any wideband-signal claim.

cards.label: BENCHMARK
cards.claim: HSC-Y3 cosmic shear finds a constant w consistent with a cosmological constant, a 2.4σ preference for dynamical dark energy, and S₈ ≈ 0.77.
cards.people: Shreya Mukherjee, Surhud More; affiliations not in source
cards.stage_headline: Stage 3 of 5: tested against a control.
cards.stage_note: This is a model comparison on independent lensing data. To be submitted to PRD.
cards.impact_text: Any dark-energy-free or modified-gravity explanation, such as backreaction or running-vacuum models, must reproduce S₈ ≈ 0.77 as well as the distances.

details.heading: What the work shows
details.text: Constant-w model: w = −0.936 (+0.074/−0.067). Time-varying model: w₀ = −0.832, w_a = −1.23, a 2.4σ preference for dynamical dark energy. S₈ ≈ 0.77 in both models.

details.heading: Keep in mind
details.text: The authors say the dynamical signal is "driven primarily by the geometric distance ladders", not by structure growth.

cards.todo: Store as a benchmark for dark-energy alternatives.
cards.compare_text: Use this as the check on Buchert's backreaction reinterpretation of DESI.

left_out: Left out: all four physics.gen-ph papers (formal theory, or a stage-1 running-vacuum exercise covered by the HSC and backreaction cards), mainstream arXiv matches that hit only on keywords, the biotechnospheres essay, four out-of-remit Retraction Watch posts, and PsyArXiv papers outside remit, including Dörner's motivation-theory "PSI" agent.
searched_note: We searched arXiv (rate-limited partway, so some abstracts were checked via search copies), PsyArXiv/OSF, JSE, Journal of Parapsychology, PLOS ONE/RSOS, Bial, PubPeer, Retraction Watch, ARPA-E, DARPA MARRS, NTRS, Galileo Project, Breakthrough Listen and the DoD UAP releases. Nothing new turned up for psi experiments, MOND galaxy or wide-binary tests, LENR primary research, Galileo Project or Breakthrough Listen, and no critiques or failed replications touched any claim in our remit.
